parameters.content: Uses the same local state file as the other workflows and expects project mappings to already exist. Keep the schedule offset behind the projects workflow. Configure the Notion Trigger node against the milestones database if you want event-driven runs.

parameters.jsCode:
const sourceTrigger = $execution.mode === 'manual' ? 'manual' : ($input.first()?.json?.body ? 'notion-trigger' : 'schedule');
return [{ json: { workflowName: 'notion-linear-milestones-sync', sourceTrigger, startedAt: new Date().toISOString(), executionId: String($execution.id || Date.now()) } }];

parameters.bodyParametersJson: ={{ JSON.stringify({ parent: { database_id: $env.NOTION_AUTOMATION_LOG_DB_ID }, properties: { timestamp: { date: { start: $json.startedAt } }, name: { title: [{ text: { content: `${$json.workflowName} pending` } }] }, details: { rich_text: [{ text: { content: 'Milestones sync started by ' + $json.sourceTrigger } }] }, status: { select: { name: 'pending' } }, workflow: { rich_text: [{ text: { content: $json.workflowName } }] }, 'execution id': { rich_text: [{ text: { content: $json.executionId } }] }, 'source trigger': { rich_text: [{ text: { content: $json.sourceTrigger } }] } } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ properties: { details: { rich_text: [{ text: { content: $json.details || 'Milestones sync finished' } }] }, status: { select: { name: $json.status || 'success' } }, 'failed node': $json.errors?.length ? { rich_text: [{ text: { content: 'Sync Milestones' } }] } : { rich_text: [] } } }) }}
